[RTCT.7.7] Per-cap enforcement points. Each entry below
defines the operation that touches the cap and the
comparison; the error returned on breach is uniform across
every row and is stated once in [RTCT.7.2]. Caps are enforced
identically in `rt` and `non-rt` engine modes when a contract
is present; the only difference between modes is pre-
allocation strategy and other RT invariants per [RTCT.12].

**The `Enumerator` column is the binding to `proto/bounds_error.proto#CapName`,
and it is carried rather than derived.** The two spellings do not correspond by
any rule: `agenda_cap` is `CAP_AGENDA`, `token_pool_cap` is `CAP_TOKEN_POOL`,
and `nodes[i].capacity` is `CAP_NODE_CAPACITY`. A gate normalising one into the
other would be a regex nobody can read, wrong in a way only a fixture would
catch, and silent
when it matched nothing. Stating the enumerator makes the reconciliation a set
difference instead.

`CAP_UNSPECIFIED` is deliberately absent from [RTCT.7.1]. It is the protobuf
zero, refused at load, and denotes no cap; `styl_5_9_2_cap_name.sql` excludes it
on the proto side for that reason, exactly as the validate registry excludes
`DS_VALIDATE_UNSPECIFIED`.
